clue.text: Use fruit one can mix for the filling

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so these letters go into the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to mix is to stir up, so the letters of one plus can are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to use fruit and a can of something mixed together as a pie filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' as a noun is the definition: an old sense of the answer is the act of putting something to use, not a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sense of the word is the act of applying or putting to use, so it can stand for use.

clue.text: A little bit soft-and continue to decay

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
to rot on is to keep decaying

explanation.surface: Something slightly soft goes on rotting.
explanation.definitionFit: This particle is a tiny constituent of every atomic nucleus, so a very little bit of matter.

clue.text: Somewhat overdue note about back-rest

indicators.note: the note goes about, or around, the other piece

parts.note: lah is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: back here means the word for rest is read backwards

parts.note: to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: An overdue note concerns a chair's back-rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-rest' looks like part of a chair, but 'back' is the reversal signal working on the word for rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The -ish suffix means rather, so the word means a little later than expected.

clue.text: Make certain of a boat on the river

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone checks that a boat really is on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee or convince someone is to make certain for them.

clue.text: Trust the company doctor in taking direction

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
E for east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone puts faith in the company doctor who is taking charge.
explanation.walkthrough: In business a trust is a group of firms joined together, the same as a cartel-like grouping.
explanation.definitionFit: A trust in commerce is a group of firms working together, also called by this name.

clue.text: A painting of the country's head

parts.note: land is country, with the possessive giving the S
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: Someone describes a picture of the nation's leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture of a rural scene or view is named for the countryside it shows.

clue.text: Glaring — and sour, too, in disposition

indicators.note: disposition is arrangement, so the letters of sour, too and in are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone is obviously, sourly bad-tempered by nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaring means blatant and widely known, as with an infamous scandal.

clue.text: Room may be found for Sid to change in 24

indicators.note: the changed letters go inside the answer to clue 24

parts.note: the answer to 24 down, meaning superior

indicators.note: change signals that the letters of Sid are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sid can find a room to get changed in.
explanation.walkthrough: A numbered reference like '24' means the answer to that clue in the grid is used as a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room flat used for both sleeping and living is a kind of room.

clue.text: State learning means a great deal

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
lore is traditional learning

explanation.surface: A state's education system is worth a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in abundance, plenty, which is a great deal.

clue.text: 11 homes — a lot anyway

definitions.note: the answer to 11 across, meaning hateful

indicators.note: anyway suggests any old way, so the letters of homes and a lot are shuffled

explanation.surface: Lots of homes are hateful, whatever you think.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean hateful or repugnant, so this one is a synonym of the answer to clue 11.

clue.text: 10 party returning credit-notes

definitions.note: the answer to 10 across, meaning detestable

indicators.note: returning means the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party
IOUs are written promises of debt, notes of credit

explanation.surface: A loathsome party hands back promissory notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean detestable, so this one is a synonym of the answer to clue 10.

clue.text: Urge to put studies before exercise

indicators.note: studies is placed ahead of the word for exercise

parts.note: to con is to study
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: A tutor is told to put study ahead of exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel or press someone is to urge them, as with being constrained to act.

clue.text: Writing in condemnation of conscription

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An article is written attacking military call-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Handwriting, or the text of a play or film, is a form of writing.

clue.text: Keeps going for brochures

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
tracts are pamphlets or brochures

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going on to fetch the leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong or drag something out is to keep it going.

clue.text: Looking put out about a seaman toiling

indicators.note: the word for scowling goes about, or around, the sailor

parts.note: louring means scowling, looking annoyed
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor looks annoyed while working hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking put out' is one phrase for scowling, an old word for which is used here.
explanation.definitionFit: Working hard at a task is toiling.

clue.text: For the numbskull it's natural to point

parts.note: simple means natural, unaffected
N for north is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Pointing is said to be natural behaviour for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish or gullible person is a numbskull.

clue.text: Regard for the bishop's province

definitions.meaning: to regard is to look at

explanation.surface: Respect is paid to a bishop's territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at or consider; a diocese, the area a bishop governs, has the same name.

clue.text: The main section of the Gene ese army

indicators.note: a section is a part, so the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The principal unit of the army of Genoa.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old poetic name for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old literary name for the ocean.

clue.text: Aim to finish

explanation.surface: Someone's goal is simply completion.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal or purpose is an aim, and to conclude or stop is to finish; both share the word.

clue.text: Understand lies are being broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast scatters things, so the letters of lies and are are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that falsehoods are going out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp or become aware of something is to understand it.

clue.text: The Romans gave him control of 17 down

definitions.text: The Romans gave him control of 17 down

parts.words: The Romans gave him control of 17 down
parts.note: Roman mythology gave rule over the ocean, the answer to 17 down, to one god

explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth he is the god of the ocean, matching the Greek Poseidon.

clue.text: A girl losing her head will get help

indicators.note: losing a head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman beheaded will need assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance or support is help.

clue.text: Tick is imperative

definitions.meaning: a tick is a moment, as in just a tick

explanation.surface: A mark or a moment is said to be urgent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a moment of time; imperative means pressing or urgent, an older sense of the word.

clue.text: Gold and copper may be seen in the village

indicators.note: gold and copper appear inside the word the

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a copper is a penny, abbreviated P

explanation.surface: Precious metals turn up in a village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be seen' is linking; copper coins mean a penny, abbreviated P in British money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old English term for a hamlet, surviving in place names.

clue.text: Man races to get in drink that's superior

indicators.note: the races go inside the drink

parts.note: beer is a drink
the TT races are held on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man who races gets in a superior drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, home of the TT (Tourist Trophy) motorcycle races, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Of higher quality means superior.

clue.text: Walk, having a street directory

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a directory

explanation.surface: Someone goes on foot with a street map in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely amble is a walk.

clue.text: Where porridge is served in a jug?

definitions.text: Where porridge is served in a jug?

parts.words: Where porridge is served in a jug?
parts.note: porridge is British slang for a jail sentence, served as time; jug is slang for jail

explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is British slang for time spent in jail, and jug is also slang for jail.

clue.text: Fool with records-they'll raise no objection

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to enter is to record

explanation.surface: An idiot with a record collection will agree to anything.
explanation.definitionFit: People who consent or agree are those who make no objection.

clue.text: A swinish trait, though it's generally accepted

parts.note: pigs are proverbially greedy

explanation.surface: Gluttony is admitted to be piggish, by common consent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everyone accepts is agreed upon.

clue.text: The guy forming designs on those who patronise him

definitions.text: The guy forming designs on those who patronise him

parts.words: The guy forming designs on those who patronise him
parts.note: designs on usually means scheming, but here the man literally draws designs onto the skin of his customers

explanation.definitionFit: He inks pictures onto the skin of the clients who pay him.

clue.text: Such a muscle requires no rest

definitions.text: Such a muscle requires no rest

parts.words: Such a muscle requires no rest
parts.note: a muscle that tightens a body part, read as one that is always tense, never at rest

explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters are also an anagram of NO REST, though no word signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the anatomical name for a muscle that tightens or stretches a part.

clue.text: About fifty deciding to get going is most unexpected

indicators.note: the word for setting off goes about, or around, fifty

parts.note: starting means setting off, getting going
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: About fifty people choosing to leave is a big surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside STARTING after its first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something highly surprising is about as unexpected as it gets.
